AI lobbying spending hit record highs last quarter, with Nvidia alone dropping $2.2 million in Washington.

As compute infrastructure scales, the balance between security, hosting reliability, and policy is shifting quickly across the tech industry.

🏛️ Nvidia, Anthropic, and OpenAI recorded their highest-spending lobbying quarters between July and September. Nvidia led the group at $2.2 million, followed by Anthropic at $2.1 million and OpenAI at $1.5 million.

☁️ Google Cloud announced Agent Compute Engine, a service providing every AI agent its own hardware-isolated microVM with no credentials inside. The platform currently runs Gemini agents and enters preview in the coming months.

⚙️ You.com launched Inference Router, an OpenAI-compatible API serving 12 open-weight models. It guarantees a 99.9% uptime SLA, zero data retention, 100% US hosting, server-side web search, and no platform fee.

🛡️ OpenAI partnered with Poland’s NASK research institute to advance AI safety and security. The partnership focuses on technical research to strengthen digital safeguards and build ecosystem resilience.

Seeing infrastructure providers introduce hardware-isolated environments for agents shows that execution security is becoming a core requirement for enterprise deployments.

At the same time, open-weight routing with guaranteed SLAs indicates that reliability standards for open models are steadily aligning with proprietary services.

Which update do you think will impact developer workflows more: dedicated microVMs for AI agents or enterprise-grade open-weight routing?
